situations: The guild hall's doors bang open; rain blows in, and a runner shouts that the east road is flooded.
A crate of supplies arrives short: half the rope and none of the lamp oil that was promised.
A notice goes up on the board: a reward for anyone who maps the old sewer under the market.
The cook drops a tray; in the quiet after, someone at the back laughs too loudly.
A stranger in a grey cloak asks the room whether anyone has been to the Sun Ruins this season.
The hearth fire dies down and nobody gets up to feed it.
A guild clerk reads out the names of three adventurers who did not come back last month.
Thunder rolls; the lamps flicker, and the map on the table curls at one corner.
A merchant offers to pay double if the party leaves at dawn instead of next week.
Someone has carved a warning into the bench: DO NOT TRUST THE FERRYMAN.
The party's packs are laid out for inspection; one waterskin is cracked.
A child slips in out of the rain and asks if this is where heroes live.
Word comes that the bridge at the river ford collapsed overnight.
A guild veteran with one arm sets down a sealed letter addressed to no one.
The rain stops all at once; through the window, the ruined towers stand very clear.
A bell in the city rings three times, which usually means a gate is closing early.
The quartermaster asks who will sign for the borrowed crossbow.
A dog wanders in, shakes itself dry over the map, and lies down by the door.
A scout reports smoke rising from the old watchtower, where no one should be.
Dawn light reaches the hall; the road out of the city is open, for now.

luke.notes: Fast, breathless sentences that trip over each other when he is nervous. Asks a question, then answers it himself. Ties things back to finding his brother.

ponticius.notes: Plain, weighty words. Wraps advice in a short story from his younger days. A bark that ends in a laugh. Never sugarcoats a risk, always offers a way forward.

arin.notes: Quick, teasing one-liners that hide worry. Says less than he means.
